versions.title_at_revision: Verify safe ground flotation capability of the landing gear systems.
versions.text: Verify safe ground flotation capability of the landing gear systems. DoD/MIL Doc: JSSG-2009 Appendix A: A.3.4.1.2.1, A.4.4.1.2.1, Ground Flotation AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.1.b Ground Flotation.

Criterion: Verify safe ground flotation capability of the landing gear systems. Standard: Landing gear systems apply loads to the airfield surface which do not exceed the bearing strength of the airfield surface for all types of airfields called out in the Operational Requirements. Method of Compliance: Verification method includes analysis. Flotation analysis verifies compliance with the flotation requirements for the given tire sizes, tire pressures and specified mission weights. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.2.1, A.4.4.1.2.1 Ground Flotation AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.1.b Ground Flotation.

Standard: The wheeled landing gear or skid landing system will prevent the air vehicle from exceeding the bearing strength of all airfield and landing surfaces (rigid, flexible or bare soil) on which the air vehicle is to operate. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis of the wheeled landing gear configuration of tire loads, tire spacing, tire pressures, and worst-case design limits of air vehicle weights and CGs, verifies the air vehicle does not exceed the bearing strength of required airfield and landing surfaces. The Aircraft Classification Number/Pavement Classification Number or Aircraft Classification Rating/Pavement Classification Rating analyses are used for rigid and flexible surfaces. Bare soil analysis is conducted using approved methods (e.g., ASD-TR-68-34, Pavement-Transportation Computer Assisted Structural Engineering).
(2) Analysis of the skid landing system configuration of loads, spacing, pressures, and worst-case design limits of air vehicle weights, and CGs, verifies the air vehicle does not exceed the bearing strength of required airfield and landing surfaces. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct tire footprint area measurements IAW MIL-DTL-5041, Footprints paragraph at rated tire pressure and tire pressure for bare soil operations, varying tire pressures and air vehicle weights to support flotation analysis. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
    (1) For air vehicles which operate on low California Bearing Ratios surfaces (i.e., semi-prepared and unprepared), conduct an air vehicle ground demonstration to verify the number of passes the air vehicle can make on the specified surfaces.
